name: Big Bear Bald Eagle Nest
seasonText: Eggs in January, chicks through June, and the pair visits the nest all year.
blurb: Home of Jackie and Shadow, the most famous eagle pair on the internet, on a Jeffrey pine high above Big Bear Lake.

name: SuperBeaks Bald Eagle Nest
seasonText: Florida eagles nest early: eggs from November, eaglets fledge by spring.
blurb: Pepe and Muhlady raise some of the earliest eaglets in the country in a longleaf pine, with alligators and sandhill cranes in the pasture below.

name: Kisatchie National Forest Eagle Cams
seasonText: Nesting October to May; canopy cams stream the forest all year.
blurb: Two wild nests deep in a Louisiana pine forest, with nest and canopy views and a devoted chat community.

name: Dulles Greenway Eagle Cam
seasonText: Eggs in February, fledging by June; the nest stays on camera all year.
blurb: A wetlands nest beside the Dulles Greenway toll road, streaming in HD with one of the longest running eagle pairs in Virginia.

name: Glacier Gardens Bald Eagle Cam
seasonText: Nesting April to August in the Tongass rainforest.
blurb: A wild nest in the mossy canopy of the Tongass, the world's largest temperate rainforest, from a botanical garden outside Juneau.

name: Hancock Wildlife Eagle Cams
seasonText: Eggs in March, fledging by August, on nests across the Fraser Valley.
blurb: The foundation that pioneered eagle streaming in Canada, rotating between wild nests around Vancouver and the Fraser Valley.

name: Glen Hazel (Hays) Bald Eagle Cam
seasonText: Eggs in February, chicks through June; the pair guards the nest all year.
blurb: City eagles above the Monongahela River, proof that bald eagles came back to Pittsburgh after a century away.

name: U.S. Steel Red-tailed Hawk Nest
seasonText: Eggs in March, young on the nest into June.
blurb: A red-tailed hawk pair nesting on U.S. Steel's Edgar Thomson plant, industry and wildness sharing one frame.

name: Cornell Red-tailed Hawks
seasonText: Eggs in March, fledging in June, above the Cornell campus.
blurb: The famous #CornellHawks nest on a light pole overlooking Cornell's athletic fields, streamed since 2012.

name: Decorah Eagles
seasonText: Eggs in February, eaglets fledge by July; eagles visit the nest all year.
blurb: The nest that started the eagle cam phenomenon, watched by hundreds of millions since 2011 beside a trout hatchery in Iowa.

name: Decorah North Eagles
seasonText: Eggs in February, fledging by July.
blurb: The second Decorah nest, in a white oak above a trout stream on a private farm north of town.

name: Trempealeau Eagles
seasonText: Eggs in February, eaglets through June, above the Mississippi River.
blurb: A bluff country nest on the Upper Mississippi, with river traffic and waterfowl drifting past below.

name: West End Bald Eagles, Catalina Island
host: Institute for Wildlife Studies on explore.org
seasonText: Eggs in February, fledging by June, on sea cliffs above the Pacific.
blurb: Eagles restored to the Channel Islands after DDT wiped them out, nesting on cliffs with the ocean glittering behind.

name: Southwest Florida Eagle Cam
seasonText: Streams October to May; eggs in November and eaglets fledge by April.
blurb: One of the most watched nests on Earth, home of the late Harriet's dynasty in a Fort Myers pasture.

name: Redding Bald Eagles (Guardian and Liberty)
seasonText: Streams during nesting, roughly February to June.
blurb: Liberty, one of the oldest known breeding eagles in the wild, raises chicks in a cottonwood beside the Sacramento River.

name: Dale Hollow Eagle Cam
seasonText: Streams during nesting, February to June, above a clear highland reservoir.
blurb: A lakeside nest on the Tennessee and Kentucky border, famous for dramatic seasons and loyal chat mods.

name: Berry College Eagles
seasonText: Streams November to May; eggs in January on the world's largest college campus.
blurb: A campus nest in tall pines watched by students and half the state of Georgia every winter.

name: Window to Wildlife Cams
seasonText: Multiple Florida nests stream through the winter breeding season.
blurb: A network of Florida nest cams, eagles and great horned owls, run with high production care.

name: Black Eagles of Selati
seasonText: Eggs April to June, chicks through spring; the cliff is active all year.
blurb: Verreaux's eagles on a granite cliff in the South African bushveld, one of very few African raptor nest cams anywhere.

name: Philippine Eagle Cam
seasonText: Streams year round from the Philippine Eagle Center.
blurb: The critically endangered national bird of the Philippines, one of the largest and rarest eagles on Earth, on camera at its conservation center.

name: California Condor Sanctuary Cam
seasonText: Condors visit the sanctuary ridge all year.
blurb: Wild California condors, back from a population of just 22 birds, soaring and squabbling on a Big Sur coast ridge.

name: White-tailed Eagle Nest, Durbe
seasonText: Eggs in March, fledging in July; the pair visits the nest all winter.
blurb: Europe's biggest eagle on a wild forest nest in western Latvia, with sound from the surrounding woods.

name: White-tailed Eagle Nest, Piotrków
seasonText: Eggs in February, young fledge by July.
blurb: Poland's Eagle Conservation Committee streams this forest nest as part of the country's remarkable eagle recovery.

name: Golden Eagle Nest, Estonia
seasonText: Eggs in March, fledging in July; eagles attend the nest in winter too.
blurb: A wild golden eagle nest in an Estonian bog forest, from the club that has streamed protected raptors since 2007.

name: Lesser Spotted Eagle Nest, Estonia
seasonText: On the nest April to August, then away to African winter grounds.
blurb: One of the world's only streamed nests of this secretive migratory eagle, deep in Estonian farmland forest.

name: RSPB Goshawk Nest Camera
seasonText: Nesting March to July in ancient Caledonian pinewood.
blurb: The phantom of the forest on a rare public nest camera in the old pines of Abernethy.

name: Hellgate Ospreys
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / University of Montana
seasonText: On the nest April to September, then away south for the winter.
blurb: Iris, the world's oldest known wild osprey, has fished the Clark Fork River from this nest for decades.

name: Charlo Osprey Nest
seasonText: On the nest April to September beneath the Mission Mountains.
blurb: An osprey platform with the snowcapped Mission Mountains behind, one of the prettiest backdrops in cam land.

name: Chesapeake Conservancy Osprey Cam
seasonText: Tom and Audrey return in March and fledge young by August.
blurb: The bay with the highest breeding osprey density on Earth, watched from a waterfront platform on Kent Island.

name: Moraine State Park Osprey Cam
seasonText: On the nest April to September over Lake Arthur.
blurb: A reintroduction success story: ospreys nesting again over a lake where the species vanished for decades.

name: SuperBeaks Osprey Nest
seasonText: Florida ospreys stay year round; eggs come as early as December.
blurb: Felix and Margareet on a Florida platform where the fishing never stops and the season starts before the new year.

name: Rogers Place Osprey and Goose Nest
seasonText: Ospreys May to September; a Canada goose often claims the platform first in spring.
blurb: A downtown Edmonton platform with an annual osprey versus goose real estate drama above the hockey arena.

name: Savannah Osprey Nest
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Skidaway Audubon
seasonText: Streams during nesting, March to July, in the Lowcountry live oaks.
blurb: An osprey nest draped in Spanish moss on Skidaway Island, with painted buntings in the marsh nearby.

name: Loch of the Lowes Osprey Cam
seasonText: On the nest late March to early September, then off to West Africa.
blurb: A Perthshire loch nest streamed since the days of the legendary female Lady of the Loch, 24 hours with night vision.

name: Loch Arkaig Osprey Cam
seasonText: Louis and Dorcha hold the nest April to early September.
blurb: A Caledonian pinewood nest in the western Highlands, one of the best loved osprey streams in Britain.

name: RSPB Loch Garten Osprey Cam
seasonText: On the nest April to early September.
blurb: The nest where ospreys famously returned to breed in Britain in 1954, still streaming from the same forest.

name: Dyfi Osprey Project
seasonText: Idris and Telyn breed April to early September on the Dyfi estuary.
blurb: Wales's flagship osprey nest in 4K, with some of the best commentary and science communication in the cam world.

name: Glaslyn Osprey Cam
seasonText: On the nest late March to September beneath Snowdonia.
blurb: The longest occupied osprey nest in Wales, guarded around the clock by volunteers in the Glaslyn valley.

name: Rutland Water Ospreys, Manton Bay
seasonText: On the nest late March to September.
blurb: The nest at the heart of England's osprey reintroduction, source of the birds now breeding in Wales and Poole.

name: Poole Harbour Osprey Cam
seasonText: CJ7 and 022 breed April to early September.
blurb: The first ospreys to breed on England's south coast in almost 200 years, with aerial and landscape views.

name: Loch Doon Osprey Cam
seasonText: Streams while the nest is active, April to early September.
blurb: A quieter Scottish nest on a moorland loch, streamed by the local council's countryside team.

name: Taipalsaari Osprey Cam
seasonText: On the nest April to late August above the Saimaa lakeland.
blurb: A Finnish lakeland nest under the midnight sun, where the fishing grounds stretch across Lake Saimaa.

name: Osprey Nest, Jedwabno
seasonText: On the nest April to early September.
blurb: One of Poland's few remaining osprey pairs, part of a national effort to bring the species back from the brink.

name: Port Lincoln Osprey Cam
seasonText: Eggs in September, chicks fledge by January; the pair stays all year.
blurb: Australia's famous osprey barge nest, streaming a southern hemisphere season that runs opposite to the north.

name: Cal Falcons, UC Berkeley Campanile
seasonText: Eggs in March, chicks fledge in June; falcons roost on the tower all year.
blurb: Peregrines on the bell tower at UC Berkeley, the cam that made Annie the falcon a Bay Area celebrity.

name: Chesapeake Peregrine Falcon Cam
seasonText: Eggs in March, fledging by June.
blurb: A peregrine eyrie above the Chesapeake, from the conservancy that also streams the bay's ospreys and herons.

name: Great Spirit Bluff Falcons
seasonText: Nesting March to July on a cliff above the Mississippi; highlights play off season.
blurb: Wild peregrines on a river bluff, complete with dramatic flycatcher neighbours and cliff swallow flybys.

name: American Kestrel Nest Box
seasonText: Streams during nesting, April to July.
blurb: North America's smallest falcon raising a family inside a prairie nest box, in partnership with kestrel researchers.

name: Common Kestrel Nest, Skrīveri
seasonText: Eggs in May, young fledge by August.
blurb: A Latvian kestrel box with the country's typical mix of crisp picture, forest sound and patient chat regulars.

name: Common Kestrel Cam, Tel Aviv
seasonText: Kestrels nest February to June; the ledge stays busy all year.
blurb: Urban kestrels on a school ledge in Tel Aviv, part of Israel's remarkable Charter Group cam network.

name: Robert E Fuller: Fotherdale Cams
seasonText: Streams all year; owl nesting peaks March to July.
blurb: The wildlife artist's Yorkshire valley, wired with dozens of cameras: barn owls, kestrels, tawny owls and the odd stoat.

name: Robert E Fuller: Ash Wood Cams
seasonText: Streams all year; tawny owls call and court through autumn and winter.
blurb: A second Fuller valley of cameras in a Yorkshire wood, with tawny owls, buzzards and badgers sharing the stage.

name: Bonnie and Clyde, Great Horned Owls
seasonText: Eggs in February, owlets through May; the box is watched all year.
blurb: The viral Kansas farm owl box where Bonnie and Clyde raise owlets above the wheat fields.

name: Barn Owl 4K Cam, Israel
seasonText: Nesting February to July; owls roost in the box year round.
blurb: Israel uses barn owls instead of rodent poison across its farmland, and this 4K box shows the program's stars up close.

name: Little Owl and Jackdaw Cam, Israel
seasonText: Little owls nest March to June and use the site all year.
blurb: A stone ruin shared by little owls and jackdaws, with the owls' glare doing most of the talking.

name: American Barn Owl Cam, Florida
seasonText: Florida barn owls can nest in any month; winter is busiest.
blurb: The Israeli barn owl research network's American outpost, streamed with the University of Florida.

name: Eurasian Eagle-Owl Cam, Riga
seasonText: Eggs in March, owlets through June; the owls hold territory all year.
blurb: Europe's largest owl breeding in the forests on Riga's edge, huge orange eyes glowing on the night camera.

name: Burrowing Owls at Umatilla
seasonText: Owls at the burrows March to September.
blurb: A colony of burrowing owls on a former army depot, bobbing and glaring at ground level.

name: Long-eared Owl Nest
seasonText: Nesting March to June; the institute keeps a camera on the site year round.
blurb: One of the world's only long-eared owl cams, from the researchers who know this secretive species best.

name: Arctic Snowy Owl Nest Cam
seasonText: Streams June to August, while the tundra nest is active under 24 hour daylight.
blurb: A snowy owl nest on the Arctic tundra at the northern tip of Alaska, one of the rarest views in the cam world.

name: Great Gray Owl Nest
seasonText: Streams April to July while the phantom of the north is nesting.
blurb: The tallest owl in North America on a broken topped snag in Montana conifer forest.

name: Charlo Great Horned Owl Cam
seasonText: Streams during nesting, March to June.
blurb: Great horned owls nesting near the osprey platform at Charlo, often on camera before the snow melts.

name: Barred Owl Nest Box
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Wild Birds Unlimited
seasonText: Streams during nesting, March to May.
blurb: A suburban backyard nest box where barred owls raise fluffy grey owlets on camera each spring.

name: Wildflower Center Great Horned Owls
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
seasonText: Streams during nesting, February to May, in a planter on a public building.
blurb: Athena the great horned owl nests in a wall planter at a busy botanic garden, unbothered by the visitors below.

name: Cornell Lab FeederWatch Cam
seasonText: Streams all year; winter brings the biggest feeder crowds.
blurb: The classic feeder cam at Sapsucker Woods, the easiest place on the internet to learn eastern North American backyard birds.

name: Ontario FeederWatch Cam
seasonText: Streams November to April, when boreal finches mob the feeders in the snow.
blurb: A deep snow Canadian feeder where grosbeaks, redpolls and Canada jays crowd the trays at 40 below.

name: Pennsylvania Bird Feeder Cam
seasonText: Streams all year with feeders topped daily.
blurb: A busy Pennsylvania feeder array in HD, with chat regulars who can name every returning bird.

name: Purple Martin House Cam
seasonText: Martins occupy the colony April to August, then leave for Brazil.
blurb: Inside a purple martin colony house, North America's most people dependent songbird raising young in an apartment block.

name: Ash Canyon Bird Sanctuary
host: Southeastern Arizona Bird Observatory on explore.org
seasonText: Streams all year; hummingbird variety peaks April to September.
blurb: A legendary sky island feeding station where fifteen hummingbird species have appeared in a single year.

name: West Texas Hummingbird Feeders
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / West Texas Avian Research
seasonText: Busiest March to October, when a dozen hummingbird species pass through the Davis Mountains.
blurb: Two dozen feeders in the West Texas mountains, a hummingbird migration highway in miniature.

name: Simi Valley Hummingbird Cam
seasonText: Streams all year; Anna's hummingbirds never leave southern California.
blurb: Carole Turek's home feeder station, headquarters of a channel devoted to filming every hummingbird species on Earth.

name: RSPB Swift Nest Camera
seasonText: Swifts occupy the nest May to early August, then fly to Africa without landing for months.
blurb: Inside a swift nest box, a close view of a bird that eats, sleeps and mates on the wing.

name: Farmer Derek Feeder Cam
seasonText: Streams all year on the farm.
blurb: The feeder end of the viral Kansas owl farm, prairie birds against a backdrop of wheat and weather.

name: Beleef de Lente (Experience Spring)
seasonText: Ten nest cams stream March to July every spring.
blurb: The Netherlands' beloved spring tradition: storks, owls, kestrels and songbirds nesting live across ten cameras.

name: Panama Fruit Feeder Cam
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Canopy Lodge
seasonText: Streams all year; fresh fruit goes out every morning.
blurb: A banana buffet in a Panamanian mountain valley where tanagers, aracaris and chachalacas parade all day.

name: Panama Hummingbird Feeder Cam
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Canopy Tower
seasonText: Streams all year in rainforest at the edge of the Panama Canal.
blurb: Jewel colored hummingbirds swarming feeders beside the Panama Canal, a dozen species on a good morning.

name: Sachatamia Lodge Hummingbird Cam
seasonText: Streams all year in Andean cloud forest.
blurb: Cloud forest feeders in the world hummingbird capital, sylphs and brilliants flashing through the mist.

name: Peru High Andes Hummingbird Cam
seasonText: Streams all year high in the Andes.
blurb: The giant hummingbird, the sword-billed and the shining sunbeam at one Andean feeder, three of the strangest hummingbirds alive.

name: BirdSouls Colombia Feeder Cam
seasonText: Streams all year from the world's birdiest country.
blurb: A fruit feeder in Colombia, the country with more bird species than any other on Earth.

name: Toucan TV
seasonText: Streams all year in rainforest canopy.
blurb: Toucans at eye level in the Costa Rican canopy, exactly as ridiculous and wonderful as that sounds.

name: Macaw Recovery Network Feeder
seasonText: Streams all year at a macaw conservation site.
blurb: Wild macaws crashing a conservation feeder in full colour, from the team restoring Costa Rica's great green macaws.

name: Great Green Macaw Nest
seasonText: Nesting December to June; the cavity is monitored year round.
blurb: A nest cavity of one of the world's rarest macaws, fewer than a thousand of which remain in the wild.

name: Lance-tailed Manakin Cam
seasonText: Streams February to July, when males dance in pairs on their display perch.
blurb: Two male manakins performing synchronized leapfrog dances for females, one of nature's strangest duets.

name: Royal Albatross Cam (Royal Cam)
host: NZ Department of Conservation / Cornell Lab
seasonText: Eggs in November, chicks on camera from late January until they fledge in September.
blurb: The world's only mainland royal albatross colony, following one nest through a whole year from egg to fledging.

name: Puffin Loafing Ledge
seasonText: Puffins crowd the ledge April to August, then head out to sea for winter.
blurb: Dozens of puffins loafing on a Maine ledge, on the island where Project Puffin brought the species back.

name: Puffin Burrow Cam
seasonText: A pufflin grows up on camera June to August.
blurb: Inside a puffin burrow, watching a single chick from hatch to its nighttime dash for the sea.

name: Guillemot Burrow Cam
seasonText: Chicks in the burrow June to August.
blurb: The puffin's crimson footed cousin raising chicks under the boulders of Seal Island.

name: Stony Point Penguin Colony
seasonText: Penguins are in the colony all year; chicks peak March to August.
blurb: One of the largest land based colonies of the endangered African penguin, braying and waddling on the Cape coast.

name: Magellanic Penguin Nest, Patagonia
seasonText: Streams October to February, the Patagonian breeding season.
blurb: A burrow nest on a wild Patagonian island, from the team rewilding Argentina's coastal steppe.

name: Southern Giant Petrel Colony
seasonText: Streams November to March while the colony raises chicks.
blurb: The vulture of the Southern Ocean nesting on a bare Patagonian island few humans ever visit.

name: Imperial Cormorant Colony
seasonText: Streams November to February at the height of the colony.
blurb: Hundreds of blue eyed imperial cormorants packed onto a Patagonian islet, a seabird city in miniature.

name: Bermuda Petrel (Cahow) Cam
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Nonsuch Expeditions
seasonText: Streams January to June, inside the burrow of a bird once thought extinct for 300 years.
blurb: The cahow, rediscovered in 1951 after three centuries presumed extinct, raises a single chick on camera each spring.

name: White-tailed Tropicbird Cam
host: Cornell Lab Bird Cams / Nonsuch Expeditions
seasonText: Streams May to September while the longtail chick is in the nest.
blurb: Bermuda's beloved longtail nesting in a cliff hole above turquoise water.

name: Mississippi River Flyway Cam
seasonText: Streams all year; spring and autumn migration bring tens of thousands of birds.
blurb: A camera on America's greatest bird highway, where pelicans, swans and eagles pour through on migration.

name: Sacramento National Wildlife Refuge Cam
host: US Fish and Wildlife Service on explore.org
seasonText: Streams all year; winter floods the refuge with a million waterfowl.
blurb: Central Valley wetlands that host one of the great waterfowl spectacles in North America every winter.

name: Great Blue Heron Nest
seasonText: Nesting March to July in a waterfront colony.
blurb: Gangly heron chicks growing up in a treetop nest over the Chesapeake.

name: Rowe Sanctuary Crane Cam
seasonText: Streams February to April, when half a million sandhill cranes roost on the Platte.
blurb: The largest crane gathering on Earth, a river of birds at dawn that people travel continents to see.

name: Decorah Goose Cam
seasonText: Streams March to May, ending with the goslings' famous leap from the nest.
blurb: A Canada goose nesting high in a hollow tree, and one day each spring the goslings jump.

name: Lesser Flamingos at Kamfers Dam
seasonText: Flamingos are present most of the year; breeding follows the rains.
blurb: Tens of thousands of lesser flamingos turning a South African dam pink, one of only a few breeding sites in the world.

name: Okaukuejo Waterhole, Etosha
seasonText: Streams all year; the dry season, May to November, packs the waterhole.
blurb: Etosha's famous floodlit waterhole, where sandgrouse and hornbills share the water with elephants and rhinos.

name: Namib Desert Waterhole
seasonText: Streams all year; mornings and evenings are busiest at the water.
blurb: A desert waterhole near Sossusvlei where weavers, korhaans and oryx appear out of an ocean of sand.

name: Kalahari Desert Cam
seasonText: Streams all year in the red dunes.
blurb: Red sand, camelthorn trees and the constant chatter of sociable weavers at their haystack nests.

name: Kwando River Cam
seasonText: Streams all year on a lush Caprivi riverbank.
blurb: A green riverside corner of Namibia alive with kingfishers, jacanas, bee-eaters and drinking elephants.

name: Tembe Elephant Park Waterhole
location: Tembe Elephant Park, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
seasonText: Streams all year with sound; over 340 bird species live in the park.
blurb: The classic African waterhole cam, hornbills and guineafowl threading between the biggest tusked elephants in Africa.

name: Nkorho Bush Lodge Cam
seasonText: Streams all year beside the Kruger ecosystem.
blurb: A Sabi Sand pan where rollers and drongos work the foreground while lions and leopards pass behind.

name: Deteema Springs Cam
seasonText: Streams all year; the dry months, July to October, bring constant traffic.
blurb: A remote Hwange spring where storks, vultures and oxpeckers attend the great herds.

name: Angama Mara Cam
seasonText: Streams all year above the Mara; the wildebeest migration passes July to October.
blurb: The view from the Oloololo escarpment across the Maasai Mara, crowned cranes and starlings in the foreground.

name: Tortilis Camp Waterhole, Amboseli
seasonText: Streams all year with Mount Kilimanjaro on clear mornings.
blurb: A waterhole under Kilimanjaro where cranes and whistling ducks feed beneath the mountain's snows.

name: Black Stork Nest, Riga Forests
seasonText: On the nest April to August, then away to Africa.
blurb: Europe's shyest stork nesting in old growth forest, a bird most birders never see in the wild.

name: Black Stork Nest, Estonia
seasonText: On the nest April to August.
blurb: The legendary Estonian black stork cams, streamed from wild forest since 2007 and narrated by a devoted forum.

name: Black Stork Nest, Bolewice
seasonText: On the nest April to August.
blurb: A Polish forest nest of the secretive black stork, streamed by the national eagle conservation committee.

name: White Stork Nest, Tukums
seasonText: On the nest April to August, bill clattering included.
blurb: The classic European village stork nest, clattering greetings on a Latvian rooftop.

name: Knepp White Stork Cam
seasonText: Streams April to August, when the storks nest in the rewilded oaks.
blurb: The first white storks to breed in Britain in 600 years, on the famous Knepp rewilding estate.

name: Storchennest Großefehn
seasonText: Streams March to August while the pair raises chicks.
blurb: A village stork nest in East Frisia, part of Germany's dense network of local stork cameras.

name: European Roller Nest Box
seasonText: Rollers occupy the box May to August, then migrate to Africa.
blurb: Italy's turquoise jewel of farmland, nesting in a research box with inside and outside views.

name: Bella Hummingbird Nest
seasonText: Bella nests October to May; between broods the cam plays calming highlights.
blurb: A hummingbird nest the size of a golf ball, and the most soothing close up in the cam world.

name: Texas Titmouse Nest Box
seasonText: Streams during nesting, March to June.
blurb: Inside a Texas nest box from egg to fledge, part of a backyard wired for wildlife.

name: Sydney Sea-EagleCAM
seasonText: Eggs in June, chicks fledge by November; the pair visits year round.
blurb: White-bellied sea-eagles nesting in an ironbark forest inside Sydney, streamed by BirdLife Australia since 2009.
